title: Unique identifier linking through account registration
description: Homeowner provides unique identifiers (email, username, device IDs) during account registration and device enrollment, enabling linking of data across sessions and systems.
assumptions: Registration requires unique identifiers for account and device identification

title: Quasi-identifier linking through combined account and device data
description: Home Hub processes combination of account information and enrolled device data, creating quasi-identifiers that can link multiple data points to the homeowner.
assumptions: Home Hub stores and correlates account and device enrollment data

title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: Homeowner shares identified personal information (name, email, contact details) during account registration process.
assumptions: Account registration requires personally identifiable information

title: Device identifier processing
description: Home Hub processes unique device identifiers from enrolled cameras and sensors, which can be used to identify the homeowner's devices and potentially infer identity.
assumptions: Cameras/sensors have unique identifiers that are transmitted during enrollment

title: Attributable registration data evidence
description: Registration and device enrollment creates data records that can be attributed to the homeowner, preventing denial of account creation or device enrollment.
assumptions: Home Hub maintains logs/records of registration and enrollment activities

title: Observed registration communications
description: The registration and device enrollment data flow could be observed by network monitors, revealing that a homeowner is registering and what devices are being enrolled.
assumptions: Data flow is observable on the network without encryption or with compromised encryption
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the flow is encrypted in transit

title: Sensitive data type disclosure during registration
description: Homeowner discloses sensitive personal data types during account registration that may exceed what is functionally required for basic account creation.
assumptions: Registration form collects more data than minimally necessary

title: Extended data retention for account and device data
description: Home Hub may retain account registration and device enrollment data longer than functionally needed for the service.
assumptions: No clear data retention policy or data is kept indefinitely
uncertainty_note: Depends on Home Hub's retention policies

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected, processed, or stored during account registration and device enrollment.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Limited data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent choices for how their personal data is processed during and after registration.
assumptions: Registration process offers limited or no granular consent options

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Home Hub may collect and process more personal data than actually needed for account registration and device enrollment functionality.
assumptions: Data collection exceeds functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices

title: Guest access code linked to identity
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be unique and logged by the Home Hub, creating a link between the code and the guest's identity or session. If the Home Hub maintains records of which codes were used and when, this enables linking the guest to specific access events.
assumptions: The Home Hub logs access code entries with timestamps and potentially associates them with guest information

title: Access code serves as identifier
description: The temporary access code may function as a unique identifier for the guest. If the code is unique to a specific guest or session, the Home Hub can use it to identify or distinguish the guest from others.
assumptions: The temporary access code is unique per guest or session

title: Access event attributable to guest
description: The Home Hub's logging of the access code entry creates data evidence that can attribute the door unlock action to the guest, preventing them from denying they accessed the property.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains logs of access code entries and door unlock events

title: Guest presence detected through door unlock
description: The application side effect of unlocking the door reveals the guest's presence and action. The Home Hub's response (unlocking) is a detectable event that indicates the guest was present and attempted access.
assumptions: The door unlock event is logged or observable

title: Access code data retained longer than needed
description: If the Home Hub retains the temporary access code or associated logs longer than necessary for the access control function, this constitutes excessive data retention. Temporary codes should be invalidated and deleted promptly after use.
assumptions: The Home Hub may store access code logs beyond the immediate access event
uncertainty_note: Depends on Home Hub's data retention policy

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest may not be aware that their access code entry is being logged, stored, or processed by the Home Hub beyond the immediate door unlock function. They may not understand what data is collected or how long it is retained.
assumptions: Guests are not informed about data processing practices for access codes

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: If the Home Hub collects or retains more data than necessary (e.g., storing access codes longer than needed, logging unnecessary metadata), this may violate the GDPR data minimization principle.
assumptions: The Home Hub may process or store data beyond what is functionally required for access control
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data processing practices

title: Profiling through sensor event patterns
description: Motion/door/sensor events stored in the local event log can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns, such as daily routines, presence times, and room usage patterns.
assumptions: The event log retains sufficient temporal and spatial detail to enable behavioral analysis

title: Revealing attributes in sensor events
description: Sensor events contain revealing attributes (timing, location, type of event) that can support identification of data subjects through pattern analysis of their movements and presence.
assumptions: Events are timestamped and location-tagged with sufficient granularity

title: Attributable presence evidence
description: The event log creates data records that can be used to prevent individuals from denying their presence or activities at specific times and locations.
assumptions: Events are logged with sufficient detail to attribute to specific individuals or households

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Motion/door/sensor events are sensitive data types that reveal personal presence and movement patterns, which may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic logging.
assumptions: The system collects all sensor events without filtering for necessity

title: Excessive data retention
description: Event logs may be retained longer than functionally necessary, increasing privacy risk over time as historical movement patterns accumulate.
assumptions: No automatic retention policy limits how long events are stored

title: Unawareness of sensor data collection
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their movements and presence are being continuously logged by the Home Hub and stored in the event log.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about the extent of sensor event logging

title: Lack of data subject preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences about which sensor events are logged, how long they are retained, or what data is collected.
assumptions: No user interface or mechanism exists for configuring logging preferences

title: Data minimization violation
description: Collecting all motion/door/sensor events may violate the data minimization principle if not all events are necessary for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: The system does not filter or limit sensor event collection to only what is functionally required

title: Unique identifier linking through video metadata
description: Home Hub includes unique identifiers (device ID, user account ID, timestamps) in video clip metadata that can be used to link data across systems and time periods.
assumptions: Video files contain standard metadata fields with identifying information

title: Profiling individuals through video analysis
description: Cloud video storage may analyze recorded clips to profile individuals based on their activities, movements, and behaviors captured in the video content.
assumptions: Cloud storage system has capability to process/analyze video content

title: Processing of identified data in video content
description: Video clips contain identifiable information such as faces, license plates, and other personal identifiers that are processed and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video clips capture identifiable individuals or objects

title: Revealing attributes in video data
description: Video content includes revealing attributes (locations, activities, associations) that support identification of data subjects beyond explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Video captures contextual information about individuals

title: Video data as attributable evidence
description: Stored video clips can be used as evidence to prevent individuals from denying their presence, actions, or claims about specific events.
assumptions: Video data can be retrieved and used as evidence

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The upload of video clips to cloud storage can be detected through network monitoring, revealing that video data transfer is occurring.
assumptions: Network traffic can be monitored

title: Sensitive video data type collection
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may exceed what is functionally required, especially if all recordings are uploaded regardless of content.
assumptions: All recorded clips are uploaded without filtering

title: Excessive video data retention
description: Video clips may be stored in cloud storage longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risks over time.
assumptions: Retention policies may not align with functional requirements

title: Data exposure to cloud storage provider
description: Video data is made accessible to the cloud storage provider as a predetermined party, which may exceed what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud provider has access to stored video data

title: Unawareness of video data processing
description: Individuals captured in video clips may not be aware their personal data is being recorded, uploaded, and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: People in video range are not notified of recording

title: Lack of control over video data erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their video data stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Data subject rights mechanisms may be limited

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing all video clips in cloud storage may process more personal data than actually needed for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Not all video content is functionally necessary

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be stored longer than needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention periods may exceed functional necessity

title: Sensitive motion data collected
description: Motion alert data reveals presence and movement patterns within the home, which is highly sensitive personal data that may exceed what is functionally required for simple alert notification.
assumptions: Motion data includes timestamp and location within home that reveals occupancy patterns

title: Linking through unique identifiers in transit
description: The motion alert flow likely contains unique identifiers (device ID, user ID, home ID) that can be used to link this data to a specific individual or household during transmission.
assumptions: Motion alerts include identifying information to route to correct user

title: Observed communications reveal activity
description: Network monitoring of the data flow could detect when motion alerts are being sent, revealing that motion was detected in the home at specific times.
assumptions: Network traffic can be observed by third parties

title: Profiling through motion pattern analysis
description: The mobile app backend can analyze motion alert data over time to profile individual behavior patterns, such as when residents are home, their movement routines, and daily schedules.
assumptions: Backend stores and processes motion data over time for analysis

title: Revealing attributes from motion data
description: Motion data contains revealing attributes (timestamps, frequency, location within home) that support identification of data subjects and their behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Motion alerts include sufficient detail to infer individual presence and behavior

title: Excessive frequency of motion data processing
description: Real-time motion alerts result in frequent processing of personal data, potentially more frequently than functionally needed for the alerting purpose.
assumptions: Motion alerts are sent in real-time for every motion event

title: Lack of user control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their motion data is processed, stored, or shared by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: System does not provide granular consent controls for motion data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing motion data for alerts may involve collecting more personal data than actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Motion data includes more detail than necessary for simple alert notification
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data fields included in motion alerts

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications sent to the homeowner can be analyzed to profile their presence patterns, daily routines, and occupancy habits. The backend processes motion data and sends notifications that reveal when and how often motion is detected at the property.
assumptions: The backend retains or processes motion detection data beyond immediate notification purposes

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes and sends notifications to a specifically identified homeowner, requiring the system to maintain and use identified data to route notifications correctly.
assumptions: The system maintains user accounts with identifiable information

title: System response reveals motion detection
description: The notification itself is a system response that reveals motion was detected at the homeowner's property, potentially exposing occupancy status and activity patterns.
assumptions: The notification content or timing reveals motion detection events

title: Sensitive motion data disclosure
description: Motion detection data is sensitive as it reveals occupancy patterns, presence/absence, and activity within the property. This data type may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic security notifications.
assumptions: Motion detection data reveals detailed occupancy and movement information

title: Excessive granularity in motion notifications
description: Notifications may include more granular details than necessary (exact timing, frequency, location within property) beyond what is needed for basic security awareness.
assumptions: Notifications include detailed motion detection metadata

title: Limited homeowner control over notification preferences
description: Homeowners may lack control over what motion detection data is processed, how frequently notifications are sent, or what details are included in notifications.
assumptions: The system does not provide granular notification preference controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If motion detection data is collected and processed beyond what is necessary for security notifications, this may violate GDPR's data minimization principle.
assumptions: Motion data is retained or processed beyond notification purposes
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data retention and processing practices

title: Personal data shared with predetermined external party
description: Mobile app backend shares device-usage analytics with cloud analytics vendor EE3, a predetermined external party. This exposes personal data to a third party beyond the original app ecosystem.
assumptions: Device-usage analytics may contain or enable derivation of personal data

title: Further processing and enrichment of analytics data
description: Cloud analytics vendor may further treat, analyze, and enrich the received analytics data beyond what is functionally needed for the original purpose, potentially creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Analytics vendors typically perform additional processing on received data

title: Profiling individuals through analytics data
description: Cloud analytics vendor can analyze device-usage patterns to profile individual users, linking data to specific individuals through behavioral patterns even if data is labeled as aggregated.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient granularity to enable individual profiling
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual granularity of 'aggregated' data

title: Quasi-identifier attributes in analytics data
description: Device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (usage patterns, timing, device characteristics) that serve as quasi-identifiers enabling identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Analytics data includes multiple attributes that could uniquely identify users
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data fields included

title: Data subjects unaware of analytics data sharing
description: Users may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with external cloud analytics vendor EE3, especially if this sharing is not clearly disclosed in privacy notices.
assumptions: Privacy disclosures may not clearly explain third-party analytics sharing

title: Lack of user control over analytics sharing preferences
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: App may not provide granular consent controls for analytics sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with external vendor may involve processing more personal data than actually needed for the stated analytics purpose, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Analytics data may include more detail than functionally necessary
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual data fields and business purpose

title: Potential invalid consent for third-party data sharing
description: If user consent was not specifically obtained for sharing analytics data with cloud analytics vendor EE3, or if consent was bundled/implicit, this may constitute invalid consent under GDPR.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not be specific to third-party analytics sharing

title: Profiling through video content analysis
description: The mobile app backend processes video clips that could be analyzed to profile the homeowner's behavior, habits, daily routines, and activities. Video content contains rich behavioral data that enables pattern analysis and linking to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video content is processed beyond simple playback, potentially enabling behavioral analysis

title: Processing of identified data in video content
description: Video clips likely contain identifiable information such as faces, voices, property details, and personal belongings. The backend processes this identified data when retrieving videos for playback.
assumptions: Video content contains personally identifiable information about the homeowner and their property

title: Video metadata contains unique identifiers
description: Video metadata likely includes unique identifiers such as user IDs, device IDs, timestamps, and location data that directly reference the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Video files contain metadata with user/device identifiers

title: Highly sensitive video data processed
description: Video content is highly sensitive personal data revealing intimate details of the homeowner's life, property, and activities. Processing full video clips may exceed what is functionally required for playback.
assumptions: Video content reveals sensitive personal information about the homeowner

title: Excessive volume of video data processed
description: Retrieving and processing full video clips may involve more data than functionally needed. Partial playback or lower resolution could suffice for the intended functionality.
assumptions: Full video clips are retrieved rather than optimized for playback needs

title: Homeowner unaware of video retrieval processing
description: The homeowner may not be aware when their stored videos are retrieved and processed by the backend, including what metadata is accessed and how the data is handled during retrieval.
assumptions: Users lack visibility into backend processing of their video data

title: Lack of control over video processing preferences
description: The homeowner may lack control over how their video data is processed during retrieval, including preferences for data minimization, metadata handling, and processing scope.
assumptions: Users cannot customize how their video data is processed during retrieval

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Retrieving and processing full video clips with all metadata may violate GDPR's data minimization principle if less data could achieve the same playback functionality.
assumptions: Full video retrieval exceeds what is necessary for playback functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation details of video retrieval
